PullRequest.Title: Avoid unnecessary --numstat diff for incoming changes decorations
PullRequest.Body:
## Problem and Context

`GitIncomingChangesFileDecorationProvider.getIncomingChanges()` (in
`extensions/git/src/decorationProvider.ts`) computes the "Incoming Changes"
file badges by calling `repository.diffBetweenWithStats()`. That method runs:

```
git diff --raw --numstat --diff-filter=ADMR -z --find-renames=<threshold>% <ref1>...<ref2> --
```

The only consumer of the result, `collectIncomingChangesFileDecorations()`,
reads only `change.status`, `change.uri`, and `change.originalUri` to pick a
badge glyph (added/deleted/renamed/modified). It never reads the
`insertions`/`deletions` stats that `--numstat` computes, so that work is
always discarded.

This code path runs automatically and without debounce whenever
`historyProvider.onDidChangeCurrentHistoryItemRefs` fires, which happens on
every git write operation and on every VS Code built-in auto-fetch tick
(`git.autofetch`, default every 180s) for any repository whose checked-out
branch has an upstream.

On a large repository backed by a partial-clone or virtualized-filesystem
remote (e.g. GVFS/VFS for Git), `--numstat` forces git to read full blob
content for every added/modified/deleted path in the diff range, and each of
those reads is a lazy network fetch rather than a local disk read. We
measured this directly: on such a repository, incoming ranges touching
several thousand files took 60-200+ seconds and pulled thousands of objects
over the network, purely to compute stats that are then thrown away. Because
the handler isn't debounced, repeated ref-change events can also stack up
multiple concurrent invocations of this work.

## Changes

- `getIncomingChanges()` now calls `repository.diffBetween()` instead of
  `repository.diffBetweenWithStats()`. `diffBetween()` already exists as a
  sibling method, already returns exactly the `Change[]` shape this caller
  needs (status + uri + originalUri), and builds a cheaper diff with no
  `--numstat` and no explicit `--find-renames` flag.
- No other call sites, types, or configuration (e.g. `git.similarityThreshold`,
  rename detection) are touched; `diffBetweenWithStats()` remains available
  and unchanged for its other callers.

## Known gaps and deliberate decisions

- **Rename badge may show as added+deleted instead of renamed, for non-default
  git config** — `diffBetween()` does not pass
  `--find-renames=<git.similarityThreshold>%` the way `diffBetweenWithStats()`
  did, so incoming-change rename detection now falls back to git's own
  `diff.renames` default instead of the user's configured threshold. With
  default git and VS Code settings (`diff.renames` on, 50% threshold on both
  sides) the output is identical either way. Only a repository with
  `diff.renames` explicitly disabled, or a `git.similarityThreshold` far from
  50%, would see a renamed file decorated as separate added (`↓A`) and deleted
  (`↓D`) badges instead of a single renamed (`↓R`) badge. The set of files
  decorated as "incoming changes" is unaffected either way; only the glyph
  choice for renames can differ, and only for non-default configs. This
  tradeoff was evaluated and accepted to avoid reintroducing the
  `--numstat`/blob-hydration cost this PR removes. No follow-up is planned; a
  full fix would mean plumbing `similarityThreshold` into `diffBetween()`,
  which is a separate, larger change.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The automatic incoming-decoration refresh eagerly requested insertion/deletion statistics for every changed path even though the only consumer discarded those fields. --numstat requires content comparison and can hydrate missing blobs in partial or virtualized repositories, so the cost scales with the incoming changed-file/content set and can overlap across refreshes.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Incoming-decoration refreshes on large partial-clone or virtualized repositories could spend 60-200+ seconds and fetch thousands of objects solely for unused numstat data, delaying decoration updates and consuming network/disk I/O.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Changed line 261 calls diffBetween, whose no-path implementation executes git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=ADMR for the same triple-dot range. This preserves the Change[] metadata needed by decorations while removing --numstat output, its parser allocations, and eager per-file content/stat work.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 261 called Repository.diffBetweenWithStats from GitIncomingChangesFileDecorationProvider.getIncomingChanges. That wrapper invokes git diff with --raw --numstat and parses insertion/deletion maps, while collectIncomingChangesFileDecorations consumes only status, uri, and originalUri. The provider runs initially when enabled and on current-history-ref changes after write operations; reported measurements for large partial-clone/VFS ranges are 60-200+ seconds and thousands of hydrated objects. Blame attributes the base line to c95739960ff4c35dd0bf89ef8a8812eb377d7dfc.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial incoming-change decorations when Git decorations are enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Provider construction invokes the refresh immediately. Publishing the initial incoming-change decoration map waits for merge-base resolution and the diff subprocess; repository opening itself does not await the handler, so this is critical to badge availability but off the repository-open completion path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the common ancestor of the checked-out and upstream refs with git merge-base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One git merge-base subprocess per repository with both local and upstream refs; independent providers can run one each concurrently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly the same merge-base subprocess ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before the diff range and initial decoration map can be computed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run git diff --name-status -z --diff-filter=ADMR for the triple-dot incoming range.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One git diff subprocess per effective provider initialization; output and CPU scale with the N paths in the incoming range.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One subprocess also ran, but it used --raw --numstat plus explicit rename detection, computed line statistics for all changed paths, emitted more bytes, and allocated a numStats map that the decoration consumer never used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before initial incoming-change badges are published.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Git obtains missing objects required to evaluate the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On a cold partial clone or virtualized repository, the prior numstat command could fetch missing objects for many of the N changed paths; after the change, name/status generally needs tree metadata, with possible blob reads limited to rename detection behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old --numstat path could force full content access and per-path object hydration; the changed command removes that stats-driven fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Any lazy object hydration occurs inside the awaited diff and delays badge availability while consuming network and object-store I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R open repositories with upstream branches, each with N changed paths between merge base and upstream; effective cardinality is one merge-base plus one diff command per repository initialization, with output/decoration objects proportional to N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Within one refresh, merge-base and diff are serialized. Repository.run tracks these read-only operations but does not limit them. Providers for multiple repositories initialize independently, and async event listeners are not awaited, so initial/nearby refreshes can overlap; the diff shortens rather than creates that exposure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no result cache or in-flight coalescing. Completed ref identities suppress later unchanged events. Previously, warm local object caches still paid numstat content scanning and larger output parsing; cold partial-clone/VFS object caches could additionally hydrate missing blobs. The changed name/status diff avoids numstat work, although configured rename detection can still inspect rename candidates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path, command arguments, consumer fields, initial invocation, and absence of a read-operation limiter are explicit in repository code. The diff only removes work from this path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup delay depends on repository count, incoming range size, object locality, rename configuration, and whether decorations are enabled (default true). The removed mechanism is largest on cold partial clones; locally complete repositories still benefit from less content work and smaller parsing allocations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR preserves boundary-call cardinality and replaces unused numstat/content work with cheaper name/status metadata, reducing subprocess CPU, I/O, output bytes, parsing allocations, and cold-object hydration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Incoming-decoration refresh after commits, fetches, pulls, and enabled periodic autofetch
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Write-operation completion fires the history-ref event without awaiting decoration listeners, so decoration work is off the originating commit/fetch/pull critical path. The merge-base and diff remain on the critical path for updated badges and can compete for Git, disk, CPU, and network resources with later work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero when completed cached ref identities are unchanged; otherwise one git merge-base subprocess per effective changed-ref event per repository.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks recomputation and publication of updated incoming badges, not completion of the originating write operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read status and paths for incoming changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for unchanged completed refs; otherwise one git diff subprocess per effective changed-ref event, with work/output proportional to N incoming paths. Enabled autofetch can trigger write events every configured period (180 seconds by default when autofetch is enabled; autofetch itself defaults off).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same event issued one diff command with --numstat, eagerly calculating unused insertion/deletion counts and parsing a larger response.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks updated badge publication and consumes shared system resources off the originating write critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: extensions/git/src/git.ts diff subprocess / partial-clone object provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch missing Git objects needed by the diff command.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously up to the missing objects needed for N changed paths on cold partial-clone/VFS storage; now stats-driven per-path hydration is removed, subject only to Git's rename detection needs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Old numstat content comparison could fetch thousands of objects for large incoming ranges; the changed metadata-only command removes that cause.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Lazy fetches inside Git delay badge refresh and may create network bursts when multiple uncoalesced refreshes overlap.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: E effective changed-ref events across R repositories, each covering N incoming paths after equality suppression; subprocess count is up to 2*E*R and overlapping work is unbounded by the repository operation tracker, while per-diff data scales with N.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: GitHistoryProvider throttles its own write-operation handler to a current call plus one queued call, but the decoration event callback is async and not awaited. Its cached refs are committed only after computation, and Repository.run has no read-only limiter, so slow refreshes can overlap across events and repositories. This missing coalescing is pre-existing; replacing numstat makes each overlapping operation materially cheaper.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: After a refresh completes, equal local/remote ref identities skip subsequent unchanged events. There is no cache by range and no negative cache; a changed range is recomputed. Cold versus warm object behavior matches the initialization scenario, and the new command removes numstat-driven content hydration.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all write operations feed the throttled history update, changed refs fire the subscribed provider, the callback awaits merge-base then diff, and only status/URI fields are consumed. No added boundary or hotter placement is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Autofetch is opt-in, write frequency varies, and exact overlap depends on diff duration and event timing. Large incoming ranges and remote-backed object stores maximize the difference; the changed mechanism is still definitively cheaper for the data this consumer uses.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Event frequency, command count, scheduling, and lack of coalescing are unchanged; the PR removes discarded per-path stat computation and therefore reduces latency/resource contention on every effective refresh.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full one-file diff and traced initialization and write/autofetch refresh scenarios through merge-base, Git diff, parsing, decoration publication, cold/warm object access, and concurrency. No diff-introduced performance issue was found. The change is a verified eager-work regression fix, recorded against introducing commit c95739960ff4c35dd0bf89ef8a8812eb377d7dfc.
